label: GDP Growth (Q1 2026 / Q2 2026 / 2026 forecast)
change: Q1 2026: -0.8% QoQ, +0.2% annual (all sectors declined). Q2 2026 (July 30 release): +2.1% YoY, +1.5% QoQ seasonally adjusted — strongest quarterly rebound since Q4 2020, boosted by World Cup-related spending; services +1.5% QoQ, industry +1.6% QoQ, primary +3.3% QoQ. Full-year 2026 forecasts remain cautious: OECD 0.8% (most pessimistic), Citi 1.1%, IMF 1.6%, BBVA 1.8%, govt target 1.5%.
source: INEGI preliminary Q2 2026, July 30; OECD Economic Outlook June 3, 2026; Citi Encuesta de Expectativas May 21, 2026

label: Annual Inflation
change: -0.25pp vs June 2026 (3.37%); fourth consecutive month of deceleration (4.6% Mar → 3.12% Jul), lowest since May 2020. Back within Banxico's 3% ± 1pp target range; core inflation also returned to target.

label: Banxico Policy Rate
change: -475bp from 11.25% peak; held unchanged at both the June 2026 and August 6, 2026 meetings (5-0 vote in August) after 15 consecutive cuts through May 7. Board is assessing the impact of prior cuts amid inflation now inside the 2.0–4.0% target range; no further cuts signaled through 2027.
source: Banco de México press release, August 6, 2026; Bloomberg

label: Peso / USD Rate (MXN)
change: Trading ~16.93 MXN/USD at the Aug 24 open (prior close 16.91) — the peso has held below 17 for two straight weeks and is up 6.04% year-to-date from the 2025 close of 18.008. Year-end consensus forecasts have widened to 19.30–20.50 pesos/dollar (SHCP 19.70, Banorte 19.30, Banxico survey analysts 20.00–20.50, Citi 19.50–20.20), well above the earlier ~18.0 Citi May 21 estimate. Banxico rate at 6.50% continues to provide carry-trade support.
source: FX markets / Banco de México reference rate, August 24, 2026

label: Foreign Direct Investment (Q1 2026 Record)
change: Q1 2026 record: $23.591B (+10.4% vs Q1 2025). Highest single-quarter FDI ever. USA top investor ($10.21B). Mining +39.7%, vehicle manufacturing +20.4%. Attributed to Plan México nearshoring strategy and EU-Mexico trade agreement. Full-year 2025: $40.9B (+11% vs 2024).
source: Secretaría de Economía; announced Sheinbaum mañanera May 26, 2026

label: Unemployment Rate
change: Improved from 2.7% (Jan 2026) — near historic low. Announced Sheinbaum mañanera economic indicators, May 28, 2026.

label: Labor Poverty Rate
change: -3.2pp (from 33.9% Q1 2025 to 30.7% Q1 2026) — reported in Second Government Report, May 31, 2026
source: CONEVAL Q1 2026 / Sheinbaum Second Government Report, May 31, 2026

label: Minimum Wage Real Increase (2021–2025)
change: Highest among OECD countries over this period

label: Pemex Total Debt (USD)
change: ~$23B reduction under outgoing director Rodríguez Padilla (Oct 2024–May 14, 2026). New director: Juan Carlos Carpio Fragoso (former CFO), confirmed May 15. First credit outlook upgrade in over a decade.

label: International Tourist Arrivals (H1 2026)
change: Record for the Jan-Jun period, +7.7% YoY vs H1 2025. Includes 24.5M overnight tourists (+4.6%) and 6.6M cruise passengers (+15.2%, ~$575M cruise spending). Total tourism economic impact ~$18.78B.
source: Sectur, H1 2026 tourism balance (presented at Sheinbaum mañanera, Aug 20, 2026)
